section_summary: This section contains diplomatic despatches, staff studies, memoranda of conversation, inter-sectional conference records, and official correspondence concerning the legal status, nationality, and treatment of Korean residents in occupied Japan. SCAP and State Department officials examined proposals to permit the Korean Diplomatic Mission to register Koreans as Republic of Korea nationals and grant them foreign national status upon renouncing Japanese citizenship. General Douglas MacArthur ultimately decided against implementing the registration plan, determining that nationality and minority problems should be deferred until direct bilateral negotiations between Japan and Korea become possible.

subfiles.about: Analyzes the policy implications of registering Koreans in Japan with the Republic of Korea and recommends deferring ultimate nationality determinations to bilateral Japanese-Korean negotiations.
subfiles.summary: Recommends against general Korean registration in Japan to preserve repatriation and naturalization options, advising the Korean representative to defer action pending intergovernmental negotiations.
subfiles.title: Staff Study: Status of Koreans in Japan (Enclosure to Tokyo Despatch No. 111)

subfiles.about: Records a discussion between Richard B. Finn and Eiji Wajima regarding Japanese governmental views, law enforcement, dual nationality, and policies toward Koreans in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Finn and Wajima discuss Japanese desires to remove Koreans, agreeing that nationality questions should be deferred while maintaining Japanese legal jurisdiction and avoiding Korean registration.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation: Koreans in Japan
subfiles.to: Office of the United States Political Adviser for Japan

subfiles.about: Presents the Korean perspective on Koreans residing in Japan and proposes policy revisions regarding property transfer, nationality registration, and anti-communist organizations.
subfiles.summary: Critiques SCAP policy from the Korean viewpoint, recommending relaxed property and currency repatriation limits, recognition of Korean nationality, and support for the anti-communist Korean Residents Union.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 216: Status of Koreans in Japan

subfiles.about: Transmits State Department comments on the Diplomatic Section's study regarding the status and treatment of Koreans in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Transmits enclosed State Department comments on the May 2, 1949 study on Koreans in Japan, noting William J. Sebald's concurrence.
subfiles.title: Letter from Max W. Bishop to Cloyce K. Huston

subfiles.about: Critiques SCAP's proposed control over Japanese nationality renunciation and suggests bilateral Japanese-Korean commissions to resolve nationality status.
subfiles.from: Division of Northeast Asian Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Argues against SCAP controlling Japanese nationality renunciation, recommending direct Japanese-Korean bilateral commissions and increased encouragement for Korean repatriation.
subfiles.title: Memorandum: Comments on 'Status and Treatment of Koreans in Japan'
subfiles.to: Office of the United States Political Adviser for Japan

subfiles.about: Reports intelligence findings showing that Chinese residents, students, and diplomatic mission personnel in Japan are increasingly sympathetic toward Chinese Communists.
subfiles.summary: Draws attention to military intelligence reporting that Chinese residents, students, and Chinese Mission personnel in Japan increasingly display communist sympathies.
subfiles.title: Airgram A-165: Study of Present Attitude of the Chinese Minority in Japan

subfiles.about: Reports General MacArthur's decision to indefinitely defer action on registering Koreans in Japan and transmitting the staff study and section check notes.
subfiles.summary: Reports that General MacArthur decided against registering Koreans in Japan, preferring to leave the problem to direct negotiations between Japan and Korea.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 554: Status of Koreans in Japan

subfiles.about: Proposes comprehensive policies regarding the legal status, nationality registration, repatriation, and civil rights of Koreans residing in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Reviews Allied and Japanese policies affecting approximately 600,000 Koreans in Japan. It recommends recognizing the Korean Mission's right to register Korean citizens who formally relinquish Japanese nationality under Japanese law, while maintaining existing repatriation, deportation, and voting restrictions pending a definitive peace settlement.
subfiles.title: Memorandum for Chief of Staff: Status of Koreans in Japan

subfiles.about: Announces that Koreans refusing repatriation will be treated as retaining Japanese nationality and will forfeit Occupation court review rights.
subfiles.summary: Warns that Koreans failing to report for repatriation will be considered Japanese nationals and forfeit Occupation court review privileges.
subfiles.title: Press Release: Koreans Must Report to Reception Centers When Called or Forfeit Recognition as Korean Nationals (TAB A)

subfiles.about: Clarifies that SCAP does not compel Koreans to obtain Japanese citizenship while affirming that remaining residents are subject to Japanese law.
subfiles.summary: Clarifies that SCAP does not force Koreans to acquire Japanese citizenship, while emphasizing that remaining residents must observe Japanese laws.
subfiles.title: Press Release: SCAP Spokesman Clarifies Status and Treatment of Koreans in Japan (TAB A)

subfiles.about: Requests governmental approval of tentative policies treating unrepatriated Koreans and Formosans in Japan presumptively as retaining Japanese nationality.
subfiles.summary: Requests governmental approval of policies presumptively treating unrepatriated Koreans and Formosans in Japan as retaining Japanese nationality pending home government recognition.
subfiles.title: Radio Message C 61223 from GHQ SCAP to WARCOS (TAB B)

subfiles.about: Conveys State Department approval of proposed policy toward Koreans in Japan and states Chinese views on Formosans are being sought.
subfiles.summary: Notifies SCAP that the State Department approves the proposed Korean policy and is consulting the Chinese Government regarding Formosans.
subfiles.title: Incoming Radio Message W 89799 from WARCOS to CINCAFPAC (TAB C)
subfiles.to: Commander in Chief, Army Forces in the Pacific

subfiles.about: Communicates President Syngman Rhee's position that the Republic of Korea has not requested general repatriation but will receive troublemakers deported from Japan.
subfiles.summary: Transmits President Rhee's statement that Korea does not request general repatriation but will accept deported troublemakers, requesting future negotiations through Tokyo.
subfiles.title: Letter from Chung Han-pum to Douglas MacArthur (TAB D)

subfiles.about: Outlines proposed SCAP views on Korean repatriation, deportation, and criteria for nationality registration by the Korean Mission.
subfiles.summary: Draft diplomatic note welcoming Korean cooperation on deportations while outlining conditions under which registered Koreans renouncing Japanese nationality receive foreign national status.
subfiles.title: Draft Note to Korean Ambassador (TAB E)

subfiles.about: Transmits the Korean Diplomatic Mission's formal request regarding the legal status of Korean residents in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Transmits a formal request urging SCAP to clarify and recognize the legal status of Korean residents in Japan.
subfiles.title: Letter from Chung Han-pum to William J. Sebald

subfiles.about: Presents extensive historical and legal arguments asserting that Korean residents in Japan never legitimately acquired Japanese nationality and must be treated as Allied nationals.
subfiles.summary: The Korean Diplomatic Mission asserts that Japanese annexation was an illegal imposition and Koreans never willingly became Japanese nationals. Citing Allied wartime declarations and European precedents like Alsace-Lorraine, it formally requests that Korean residents in Japan be recognized and treated as Allied nationals.
subfiles.title: Request for Clarification of the Legal Status of Korean Nationals in Japan

subfiles.about: Provides G-1's concurrence in principle with the staff study, recommending procedures for Japanese citizenship and notification of Washington.
subfiles.summary: Concurs in principle with the staff study, recommending Japanese citizenship opportunities for non-registering Koreans and notification to State and Army.
subfiles.title: Check Sheet: Status and Treatment of Koreans in Japan (G-1 to DS)

subfiles.about: Summarizes an inter-sectional conference between DS, G-1, G-2, GS, and LS on Korean nationality, voting rights, and citizenship procedures.
subfiles.summary: Records inter-sectional agreement to acknowledge Korean registration rights and notify Washington, while exploring Japanese family register procedures to enable naturalization.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conference: DS Staff Study on Status and Treatment of Koreans in Japan
subfiles.to: Office of the United States Political Adviser for Japan

subfiles.about: Circulates the staff study for concurrence and records G-2's approval recommending careful screening of applicants by the Korean Mission.
subfiles.from: Diplomatic Section and G-2, GHQ FEC
subfiles.summary: Circulates the staff study to GHQ sections and records G-2's concurrence urging careful screening of Korean registration applicants.
subfiles.title: Check Sheets: Status and Treatment of Koreans in Japan (DS to Sections, and G-2 to DS)
subfiles.to: Legal Section, Government Section, G-1, ESS, and Diplomatic Section
